text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree prohibiting sales of strong spirits in kiosks and open markets in a move seen as a step towards introducing a full state monopoly over the alcohol industry.
- Russia and Kazakhstan have lost billions of dollars by failing to start work on an oil pipeline from the Caspian to Europe.
- Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov says reforms promoted by young newcomers to the government have a lot of shortcomings.
- The Duma deputies will decide the fate of the 1997 budget at a session on May 21.
- Verkhnesaldinsk metallurgical group will deliver more than two tonnes of titanium to U.S. company Boeing over the next two years.
- President Yeltsin's decree prohibiting street sales of strong spirits is unlikely to increase budget revenues.
